events.title: Imperial troops sack Rome
events.description: Unpaid troops of Emperor Charles V stormed Rome, killing thousands and looting churches while Pope Clement VII sheltered in Castel Sant'Angelo. The sack scattered Rome's artists and humbled the papacy.
events.html: Unpaid troops of Emperor Charles V stormed Rome, killing thousands and looting churches while Pope Clement VII sheltered in Castel Sant'Angelo. The sack scattered Rome's artists and humbled the papacy.

events.title: Konbaung armies storm the starving city of Pegu
events.description: After a siege that left the city starving, Konbaung forces broke into Pegu at moonrise and massacred men, women and children. Alaungpaya entered through the Mohnyin Gate, the walls were razed, and the fall ended the Konbaung–Hanthawaddy War.
events.html: After a siege that left the city starving, Konbaung forces broke into Pegu at moonrise and massacred men, women and children. Alaungpaya entered through the Mohnyin Gate, the walls were razed, and the fall ended the Konbaung–Hanthawaddy War.

events.title: Work begins on Bangkok's Grand Palace for King Rama I
events.description: Rama I, founder of the Chakri dynasty, ordered the palace built when he moved the capital from Thonburi to Bangkok. It has been the official residence of the kings of Siam since 1782, and the court and government were based there until 1925.
events.html: Rama I, founder of the Chakri dynasty, ordered the palace built when he moved the capital from Thonburi to Bangkok. It has been the official residence of the kings of Siam since 1782, and the court and government were based there until 1925.

events.title: Penny Black becomes valid for postage
events.description: Britain's prepaid adhesive stamps could now be used on letters. Paying a flat penny in advance, rather than charging recipients by distance, made post cheap and predictable.
events.html: Britain's prepaid adhesive stamps could now be used on letters. Paying a flat penny in advance, rather than charging recipients by distance, made post cheap and predictable.

events.title: Chester Arthur signs the Chinese Exclusion Act
events.description: The law suspended the immigration of Chinese labourers and barred Chinese immigrants from citizenship. It was the first major US law to exclude a group by nationality and was repealed only in 1943.
events.html: The law suspended the immigration of Chinese labourers and barred Chinese immigrants from citizenship. It was the first major US law to exclude a group by nationality and was repealed only in 1943.

events.title: Paris Exposition Universelle opens beneath the Eiffel Tower
events.description: The world's fair marking the centenary of the French Revolution opened in Paris. Its entrance arch, Gustave Eiffel's iron tower, was then the tallest structure in the world.
events.html: The world's fair marking the centenary of the French Revolution opened in Paris. Its entrance arch, Gustave Eiffel's iron tower, was then the tallest structure in the world.

events.title: Edward VII dies and George V becomes king
events.description: Edward VII died at Buckingham Palace after a nine-year reign. Known for his diplomacy and support for the Entente Cordiale, he gave his name to the Edwardian era.
events.html: Edward VII died at Buckingham Palace after a nine-year reign. Known for his diplomacy and support for the Entente Cordiale, he gave his name to the Edwardian era.

events.title: Hindenburg airship bursts into flames at Lakehurst
events.description: The German airship Hindenburg caught fire while mooring in New Jersey, killing 36 people. Newsreel film and radio coverage of the disaster ended public faith in passenger airships.
events.html: The German airship Hindenburg caught fire while mooring in New Jersey, killing 36 people. Newsreel film and radio coverage of the disaster ended public faith in passenger airships.

events.title: Roger Bannister runs the first sub-four-minute mile
events.description: On a windy evening at Oxford's Iffley Road track, the medical student Roger Bannister ran the mile in 3 minutes 59.4 seconds, helped by pacemakers Chris Brasher and Chris Chataway.
events.html: On a windy evening at Oxford's Iffley Road track, the medical student Roger Bannister ran the mile in 3 minutes 59.4 seconds, helped by pacemakers Chris Brasher and Chris Chataway.

events.title: Channel Tunnel is formally opened
events.description: Queen Elizabeth II and President François Mitterrand opened the 50 km rail tunnel under the Channel. It gave Britain its first fixed link to the Continent since the Ice Age.
events.html: Queen Elizabeth II and President François Mitterrand opened the 50 km rail tunnel under the Channel. It gave Britain its first fixed link to the Continent since the Ice Age.

song: German-speaking lands; later German student fraternities and the resistance to Nazism
An old German song that says no one can lock up your thoughts. People sang it against censorship and against the Nazis.
